United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: Global Histories, Shared Memories: Advancing Universal Access through Digitized UNESCO Archives and Knowledge Networks

description.narrative: Archives are vital cultural goods that benefit everyone when equal access is available. UNESCO's institutional archives and historical audiovisual collections contain 80 years of ideas and actions for peace, poverty eradication, sustainable development, and international understanding. UNESCO is also the custodian of the archives of its precursor bodies, including the International Institute of Intellectual Cooperation (IICI) transferred in 1946 and included on the Memory of the World register in 2017, and the archives of the Conference of Allied Ministers of Education (CAME) and the Preparatory Commission for the Establishment of UNESCO. The institutional archives and precursor bodies archives reflect early ideas and discourses in international intellectual cooperation in the interwar and postwar periods on subjects ranging from education, natural sciences, cinema, art, literature, archaeology, translation, libraries and archives, and more. However, despite their historical value and importance in preserving the Organization’s institutional memory, only 5% of UNESCO’s archives are currently digitized. There is an underexploited treasure that needs to be digitized and made available to the public at large. The current 5-year project will digitize a substantial portion of UNESCO’s core archives to ensure they are more accessible, visible, and appropriately preserved over the long-term. The project aims to bring these archives to the attention of the public through digitized collections published on UNESCO platforms, exhibitions, publications and other initiatives, and to the scientific community to strengthen research, and thus knowledge, of the Organization's history. The archive digitization project is an integral part of the One-UNESCO Digital Transformation Framework and Modernization Roadmap to preserve and increase the value of UNESCO’s knowledge assets and institutional memory, in line with the United Nations Data Strategy and UN 2.0.
